planting.note: Set rhizome divisions or potted plants in early spring into humus-rich, lime-free woodland soil in dappled to full shade; established clumps tolerate summer dryness better than most Maianthemum relatives.

directions: Grow in moderately fertile, humus-rich, lime-free soil that stays moist in spring but can dry somewhat by midsummer, siting plants in dappled woodland shade beneath trees or shrubs. A compact Asian cousin of the native false Solomon's seal, this rhizomatous perennial forms slowly spreading clumps of arching stems clad in broad, parallel-veined leaves, topped in spring with frothy terminal clusters of tiny starry white flowers. The blooms give way to speckled green berries that ripen red by autumn, adding a second season of interest before the foliage goes dormant. Its smaller stature compared to Maianthemum racemosum makes it a good front-of-bed companion for hostas, ferns, and epimediums in a shaded border.
